headline: Bangladesh's foreign exchange reserves cross $36 billion
summary: The country's reserves have seen a positive shift, while the government approves a Tk 1,356 crore LNG purchase and other development projects.
details: Bangladesh's foreign exchange reserves have surpassed the $36 billion mark, signaling a positive trend in the country's financial stability.
Alongside this economic update, the government has approved the purchase of Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) worth Tk 1,356 crore.
The approval for the LNG purchase is aimed at ensuring energy security and maintaining a steady power supply across the country.
Additionally, the government has given the green light to several other development projects to further stimulate national growth.
These combined moves reflect the government's focus on balancing foreign currency reserves with critical infrastructure and energy investments.

headline: Two train mishaps in Cumilla: Rail links to Chattogram cut off
summary: An engine failure on the Sonar Bangla Express and the derailment of four Meghna Express coaches disrupted one of Bangladesh's busiest routes.
details: Rail communication between Chattogram and the rest of Bangladesh was suspended on Wednesday evening after two separate incidents occurred near Hasanpur Station and in Gunabati, Cumilla.
The disruption began when the Dhaka-bound Sonar Bangla Express from Chattogram suffered an engine failure shortly after passing Gunabati Station, leaving it stranded near Hasanpur.
Following the breakdown, the Chandpur-bound Meghna Express, which had also departed from Chattogram, was routed through the down line via Gunabati Station toward Hasanpur.
During this maneuver, four coaches of the Meghna Express derailed, further complicating the situation and blocking the rail lines.
Laksam Junction Station Master Omar Faruk stated that rail services on the Chattogram route were disrupted for over an hour as recovery efforts began.
A replacement engine was dispatched from Chattogram to rescue the stranded Sonar Bangla Express, while the derailed coaches of the Meghna Express were separated to clear the line.
Train movement was expected to resume once the recovery work was completed and the lines were cleared.
caption:
Two train mishaps in one evening: an engine failure and a derailment in Cumilla have cut off rail links to Chattogram.

Rail communication between Chattogram and the rest of Bangladesh was suspended on Wednesday evening after two separate incidents occurred near Hasanpur Station and in Gunabati, Cumilla.

The disruption began when the Dhaka-bound Sonar Bangla Express from Chattogram suffered an engine failure shortly after passing Gunabati Station, leaving it stranded near Hasanpur.

Following the breakdown, the Chandpur-bound Meghna Express, which had also departed from Chattogram, was routed through the down line via Gunabati Station toward Hasanpur.

During this maneuver, four coaches of the Meghna Express derailed, further complicating the situation and blocking the rail lines.

Laksam Junction Station Master Omar Faruk stated that rail services on the Chattogram route were disrupted for over an hour as recovery efforts began.

A replacement engine was dispatched from Chattogram to rescue the stranded Sonar Bangla Express, while the derailed coaches of the Meghna Express were separated to clear the line.

Train movement was expected to resume once the recovery work was completed and the lines were cleared.
